_review.scope: Only BRIEF-12.md Part C tree sprites: 56 files. Floor bases and all approved comparison art are reference material, not verdict subjects.
_review.calibration: Good enough to ship next to approved art. Narrow conifers, broad umbrella crowns, open branching trees and short broken stumps are judged in their intended size class. No demand for extra detail merely because a sprite looks simple at 8x.
_review.previous_review: critic-r12C-1.json: 52 passes and 4 failures. SHA-256 comparison confirms that only the four failed bamboo sprites changed. All 52 unchanged passes were re-inspected; no concrete new defect warrants reversing a pass.

checks.brief_and_reference: Read BRIEF-12.md Part C and shared requirements, plus original BRIEF.md and BRIEF-2.md style rules. Viewed all eight treeline_forest sprites and their autumn counterparts at 1x and 4x.
checks.approved_art: Viewed all 24 approved markers at native size; city, industry, slums, suburb, farmland and paddies comparison boards at 4x, including seasonal versions shown on the boards. Viewed full grass/plains base swatches and all eight complete detail canvases for each of four seasons at native size. Compared palette, pixel density, dark edges, upper-left illumination and snow treatment. No new verdict on comparison art.
checks.forest_lattice_1x_4x: All seven sets were composited in deterministic staggered forests on existing appropriate forest/conifer/deadforest ground and inspected at exact native 1x and nearest-neighbour 4x. Dense overlapping portions and thinning edges both checked. No backing rectangle, per-cell seam, crown-clone pattern or unacceptable muddy overlap found.
checks.every_sprite_8x: Inspected every one of the 56 full 48x48 files at exact 8x in fourteen four-sprite sheets. Each enlarged sprite occupies its own complete 384x384 panel. No sprite was judged solely from a thumbnail.
checks.edges_and_alpha: Inspected every sprite against both light and dark backgrounds at 4x. No pale fringe, key-colour fringe, halo, clipping, blur or antialiasing found. Programmatic checks confirm 48x48 RGBA, only 0/255 alpha, zero hidden RGB, transparent outer margins and opaque bottom-centre contact at (23,44).
checks.placement_scale_light_palette: Trunk/root contact, tree size class and top-left highlights fit the treeline reference. Greens, grey deadwood and blue-white snow fit the approved context without a new palette clash. Narrow crowns and broken stumps are intentional subject variation.
checks.variation: No exact duplicates among the 56 source PNGs. Visual silhouette comparison finds meaningful species, crown-width, lean and branching differences within each set. Revised bamboo 2 and 6 are distinct from one another and from the remaining clumps. Corresponding winter layouts intentionally retain summer structure.
checks.winter: All 24 winter trees remain present and recognizable, with snow on supported branches, foliage or stump ledges. No blank winter file or inconsistent replacement layout found. Snow does not erase the revised bamboo stem channels.
checks.base_3x3: Not applicable: Part C delivers no bases. Existing floor bases are only compositing ground and were not added to the verdict scope.
checks.peak_range: Not applicable: Part C delivers no peaks. Tree forest lattice check performed for all seven sets.
checks.one_cell_random_8x2: Part C has transparent trees, not opaque edge-joining terrain tiles, so seam tiling is not a Part C requirement. Supplemental contiguous randomized 8x2 boards were saved for every set; revised bamboo summer/winter boards were additionally inspected at 1x and 4x for variant repetition and native readability.
checks.specific_problem_list: Identical crowns, noise, muddy shapes, weak bamboo structure, winter consistency and native readability checked directly. Egg-crate peaks, Swiss-cheese craters, classical ruins, stamped cyberpunk grids and flat orange autumn are outside Part C; no verdict was issued on those other subjects.

bamboo-0.notes: Several long culms and open vertical channels remain visible; small leaf sprays support the bamboo reading.

bamboo-1.notes: Sparse asymmetric sprays leave the long segmented culms readable at native size; finer leaves remain subordinate.

bamboo-2.notes: The previous closed triangular bush has been opened into several long, separately readable segmented culms. Continuous ground channels run through the upper clump; small side sprays leave the culms exposed. At 1x it reads as upright bamboo, including in mixed forest and random 8x2 proofs. No longer a single flecked crown. Pass.

bamboo-3.notes: Leaning sparse clump keeps a readable main stem structure and open, directional side sprays.

bamboo-4.notes: Open channels separate the main culms; leaf clusters remain distinct enough to read as bamboo.

bamboo-5.notes: Few tall exposed segmented culms and sparse leaves give the clearest small bamboo silhouette.

bamboo-6.notes: The former round shrub crown has been replaced by separated leaning culms and coherent downward leaf sprays. The right-heavy lean remains distinct from the upright variants, with exposed nodes and ground channels. Stems remain legible at 1x in the forest. The 8x view shows deliberate leaf clusters rather than scattered crown noise. Pass.

bamboo-7.notes: Open spreading clump retains a readable fan of segmented culms and separated side sprays.

bamboo@winter-0.notes: Several long culms and open vertical channels remain visible; small leaf sprays support the bamboo reading. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-1.notes: Sparse asymmetric sprays leave the long segmented culms readable at native size; finer leaves remain subordinate. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-2.notes: The revised open upright culms remain visible through the winter treatment. Snow rests on a few supported upper leaf sprays and does not close the vertical ground channels or turn the clump into a striped bush. Winter is populated and registered to the summer counterpart. Pass.

bamboo@winter-3.notes: Leaning sparse clump keeps a readable main stem structure and open, directional side sprays. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-4.notes: Open channels separate the main culms; leaf clusters remain distinct enough to read as bamboo. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-5.notes: Few tall exposed segmented culms and sparse leaves give the clearest small bamboo silhouette. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.

bamboo@winter-6.notes: Separate leaning culms and drooping sprays survive the snow treatment. Snow is grouped on supported upper leaves; it does not recreate the old mottled shrub mass. Green stems and dark leaf undersides stay readable against winter ground at 1x, with crisp caps at 8x. Pass.

bamboo@winter-7.notes: Open spreading clump retains a readable fan of segmented culms and separated side sprays. Supported snow caps preserve exposed green culms and readable gaps between sprays.
